body.translated_text: || <s>Vṛttamālāstuti</s> (A Hymn in a Garland of Metres) ||

children.translated_text: Metre is [classified as] even (<s>sama</s>), half-even (<s>ardhasama</s>),
and uneven (<s>viṣama</s>) — so declare the lords of speech;
for the benefit of others, [they are described]
briefly [as] threefold, [but] in detail, infinite.
Where the form is invariably fixed,
and a name has been chanted by the great sages,
that supreme syllabic unit (<s>chandaḥpada</s>)
manifests through various arrangements.
Even from the observation of corresponding patterns,
the heavy and light [syllables] can, in their full sequence,
be counted by the wise —
what more need be said about the inquiry here?
May that which is contemplated with respect by you,
O fortunate ones of noble birth,
prevail for the destruction of error —
[the science of metre], the one true ornament of speech.

that surpasses the triple world,
she alone is our
authority (<s>pramāṇikā</s>),

In the illustrious lineage of the <s>Saṃbuddhas</s>,
mighty in the destruction of intense afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>),
this fame of yours bears [its] ornament,
a garland of lightning
shining like
upon a [rain-]cloud.
Bearing the staff of a banner,
as if to teach ethics,
shines forth, [instructing] the world
the graceful play of your noble preceptorship
as if it were a young student.
Of you who proclaim the true path
of the triple world, O one of vast wisdom,
your waving palm
rivals a tender sprout.
Together with realization, simultaneously
in the essences of truth, O Supreme Lord,
your speech, marvelous,
produces the entire [teaching] —
rich in varied words.
In your vast
glory, some attain [merely] a footstep;
where even your sidelong glance,
having found its mark,
comes to rest for a moment.
From the fragrance of your gaze alone,
this [multitude] has attained worthiness;
the people shine like the earth itself,
the ploughshare of beneficence.
constantly [tilled by]
O Boon-granter, that ripening indeed arises
by which, in this [world],
the seed of your word, once sown,
a fruit whose form
is peace.
bears fruit —
Who here is capable of reckoning
your deeds, O Lord?
[They are] like the track of a young serpent
in water,
in a time of a hundred [layers of]
darkness.
Yet the joy born from hearing your fame
dispels the ruin of courage,
a seal [of delight] —
established by its own majesty,
and sets upon the world's face
O Lord!
O abode of <s>Śrī</s>, who have crossed to the far shore
your body shines in the lineage of <s>Buddha</s>-sons
of knowledge and conduct with graceful skill,
among [other] lotuses
as a lotus [shines]
born of water.
I bow to you, the rising mountain of a celebrated lineage,
the light of wisdom, seated upon the chariot of skillful means,
the sun
of the triple world's
fierce in shattering dullness,

shines greatly through your glory, O Lord,
like the summit-land of a distinguished mountain,
[gleaming] golden
with the lustre of jewel-sprouts.
Spreading everywhere your cry of victory,
the throng of the virtuous wanders, illuminating the world,
a proclamation-drum
in all directions.

dwelling in the glory of the lotus-head [of the foremost debaters],
your speech, intoxicating even the steadfast, revels
inebriated!
[throughout] the triple world —

that [state] called youth seems to fade [by comparison];
is called <s>Mayūrasāriṇī</s>

the world

with a continuous stream of incomparable, flashing beauty —
does it not produce joy in everyone,
on all sides (<s>Samantabhadrikā</s>).
O Ruler? [It is] auspicious

— stainless, bright as the autumn moon's rays —
like a garland of freed [pearls],
circular (<s>Vṛttā</s>).

welcomed

A storehouse of honey with pervasive fragrance,

the beauty of the blue lotus — reclining on soft petals,
with the play of bees.

<s>Vāsava</s> (<s>Indra</s>) alone is supremely honored,

wind and waves

of the <s>stomas</s> (hymns) of your praise, exceedingly captivating the mind —
moist with dense moonlight, fragrant with camphor,
[like a falcon] —

With many lofty, rising peaks,

[thunderbolt of] <s>Indra</s> —

with the flourishing majesty of the lord of <s>dharma</s>,
you are worshipped by those auspicious in beauty, O Lord of <s>Śiva</s>,
[in the metre] <s>Upendravajrā</s> —
by the creators of battle.
May your two feet, rich with characteristics
manifested in immediate succession, also come within the sight
of those whose eyes are [like] the elaborate plays of the audible —
(births)

Undoubtedly, even when other noble beings exist
who abundantly embody every quality of the self,
the lords desire you alone with a uniquely exclusive wisdom,
[you who are] established in the lineage
(<s>Vaṃśastha</s>).
O conqueror of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Love) —
With a youthful form, charming and variegated ornaments,
golden-hued, with <s>Akṣobhya</s> as the lord of your crest,
I bow to the Lord of Speech — embodied in the forms of speech and intellect —
(Vaṃśā of the Lord of Sages),
the glory of whose lineage's arising [shines forth].
[in the metre] <s>Maunīndravaṃśā</s>
Even with the most extensive speeches, O sweet-voiced one,
they reached not the far shore of your virtues, O Lord;
yet this praise, producing merely its own delight,
though measured in syllables,
is surely beautiful.
Praiseworthy for its resplendent full array of ornaments,
arisen from the lotus-faces of the meritorious,
O Lord of <s>Bhāratī</s> (Speech), luminous by its own nature, [the goddess]
wearing a garland of good qualities (<s>Sragviṇī</s>).
<s>Bhāratī</s> approaches you of her own accord,

the fire of hatred is pacified, the dullness of delusion is cast away;
O Lord, whose form is intent on the welfare of the triple world,
[universally shared,] <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> —
through you alone.

opponents become fearful and feeble;
they consider the easily attained state of muteness a great [mercy],
[when even] speech uttered
rapidly or slowly (<s>Drutavilambita</s>) [fails them].

(heavenly Ganges) of <s>Meru</s>'s summit.

children.translated_text: O bestower of boons, that one alone of fair face brings to his mouth [such speech],
accompanied by the <s>Yajus</s> with its honeyed <s>Sāman</s>-abode,
and this a stage-drama
is the Creator's [work].
born of the pride of being nectar to the ears—

with the joy of drinking the nectar of tranquility flowing from the clusters of your teachings—
